name: Minnesota
nameStory: From the Dakota 'mnisota' - water so clear it reflects the sky. A state named for the look of its water, in a place that has more lakes than almost anywhere on the continent.
capitalStory: Saint Paul was originally called Pig's Eye, after a one-eyed whiskey trader named Pierre 'Pig's Eye' Parrant who set up shop there. A priest built a chapel in 1841 and renamed it, which is the only reason Minnesota's capital is not Pig's Eye, Minnesota.

majorFeatures.name: Lake Itasca
majorFeatures.note: Headwaters of the Mississippi - you can step across it

majorFeatures.name: Lake Superior
majorFeatures.note: The North Shore and the port of Duluth

majorFeatures.name: Boundary Waters
majorFeatures.note: A million acres of lakes and canoe routes

majorFeatures.name: Iron Range
majorFeatures.note: Iron ore that built American steel

funFacts: The Mississippi River begins here as a stream you can walk across in about ten steps.
Minnesota actually has 11,842 lakes bigger than ten acres, so the nickname undersells it.
Water leaving Minnesota can end up in three different oceans: the Gulf of Mexico, Hudson Bay, or the Atlantic by way of the Great Lakes. Very few places on Earth drain three ways.
Iron from the Mesabi Range supplied a huge share of the steel used in World War II.
